weekly.title: Federal Judge Again Blocks Trump’s Ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
weekly.summary: The ruling will allow the outlets to enter the White House grounds while they sue to overturn the ban. But it doesn’t resolve all of their access problems.

weekly.title: As Pope Leo Recovers From Surgery, Messages of Support Abound at Rome Hospital
weekly.summary: The pontiff, 71, is expected to spend about a week in the hospital recovering from surgery that found lung cancer. Messages of support have flooded in from far and wide.

weekly.title: China’s Exports Soar, Putting Its Trade Surplus on Track for a Record
weekly.summary: China’s exports grew last month at the fastest pace in almost any month since the end of the global financial crisis.

weekly.title: Democrats Blame Trump After CPI Report Shows Energy Prices Drove Up Inflation
weekly.summary: Inflation and economic frustrations have expanded the map of competitive midterm election districts deep into Republican territory.

weekly.title: Rogue A.I. Agents from China Chatted with Researchers
weekly.summary: Researchers discovered that the agents were trying to bypass security controls on websites and made contact with them. A Times reporter was invited to join the discussion.

weekly.title: 5 Costs Americans Are Paying More for as Inflation Rises
weekly.summary: Consumers are paying more for everyday goods and services, like food, computers and streaming.

weekly.title: Here’s the latest.
African nations on ‘knife’s edge’ as US embassy warns Americans of long-range attacks
weekly.summary: With regional tensions mounting, the Horn of Africa risks war between Ethiopia and Eritrea. Following attacks in Addis Ababa, the U.S. Embassy warned citizens of long-range threats.

weekly.title: Social Security COLA for 2027 Will Be 3.6%
weekly.summary: The cost of living adjustment, or COLA, for next year will be the largest since 2023. Retirees will see the extra money in their benefit checks starting in January.

weekly.title: Gas Prices Are Up 34% From a Year Ago, Adding to Inflation Pressures
weekly.summary: Energy prices have surged since the start of war with Iran, lifting inflation in the United States.

weekly.title: Dalí Book Cover Stolen in France
weekly.summary: Three thieves broke into a private museum in central France and took off with a 330-pound book cover created by the surrealist master Salvador Dalí.

weekly.title: ‘Why Did They Kill Him?’ Mourning Victims of Houthi Attack on a Saudi Airport
weekly.summary: The strike was the Iran-backed militia’s most lethal against Saudi Arabia, by far, during their long conflict.

weekly.title: Rising Costs Push Necessities Out of Reach for Nearly Half of Americans
weekly.summary: Inflation has made basic goods hard to afford and attitudes toward inequality have changed, studies from the Pew Research Center showed.

weekly.title: From Allies to Enemies: Ethiopia and Eritrea Edge Toward War
weekly.summary: The two nations fought alongside each other during a brutal conflict in Tigray that left hundreds of thousands of people dead just a few years ago. Now they are on the brink of fighting each other.

weekly.title: Hollywood Agents and Producers Push to Restore Glory Days of Indie TV
weekly.summary: A new alliance seeks legislation to force the biggest entertainment and streaming companies to devote half of their content budgets to independent producers in the U.S.

weekly.title: Indian Protesters Describe Rough Treatment by the Police
weekly.summary: Some of those detained accused security forces of beating them during an intense crackdown on demonstrations in India’s capital over the weekend. Police have said they followed the law.

weekly.title: The Taliban Suspend BBC Broadcasts Across Afghanistan
weekly.summary: The Taliban government has intensified its crackdown on the press in recent months but had so far targeted Afghan news outlets.

weekly.title: Trump’s Latest Effort to Fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook Underscores Political Motives
weekly.summary: President Trump tapped his political appointees to determine whether he could oust Lisa Cook, a Fed governor he had already tried to oust.

weekly.title: Choosing a Medicare Advantage Provider for 2027 May Be Easier, but Not Perfect
weekly.summary: The government has made improvements to the Medicare Plan Finder, a key online tool, in time for open enrollment. It helps seniors compare policies to avoid costly surprises.

weekly.title: Argentina’s President Has a Dog Psychic. Meet Celia Melamed.
weekly.summary: In Argentina, many people try to read the mind of the president. Celia Melamed read the mind of his dogs.

weekly.title: ‘The Assassin(s)’ Movie Fuels South Korea’s Culture Wars
weekly.summary: The film, “The Assassin(s),” revisits a 1974 shooting that has spawned J.F.K.-style conspiracy theories, exposing divides over the country’s history.

weekly.title: F.B.I. Arrests OpenAI Employee Accused of Planting Bug in Office
weekly.summary: OpenAI said that the employee had placed a device built to evade detection and that he had planned to secretly record meetings in other sensitive spaces.

weekly.title: Senators Urge Trump to Reverse Diesel Deal With Putin
weekly.summary: A bipartisan group of 12 senators called on the president to drop his decision to ease sanctions on Russia’s exports of diesel fuel, saying the deal would help Moscow continue the war in Ukraine.

weekly.title: Lawyer for Fed Governor Cook Denounces Trump’s New Investigation
weekly.summary: A lawyer for Lisa Cook raised “significant concerns” over the “objectivity and fitness of the committee” assembled by President Trump as a way to remove her as a governor at the Federal Reserve.

weekly.title: Greta Thunberg joins massive French student protests as cars burn, police fire tear gas
weekly.summary: Greta Thunberg joined student protesters in France amid over 6,100 arrests and widespread school closures as violent clashes with riot police escalate.

weekly.title: NASA’s Perseverance Rover Sets a Mars Driving Record
weekly.summary: Advances in self-driving technology have made it easier to traverse distant worlds.

weekly.title: Apple Introduces HomeView, a $299 Tablet for the Home
weekly.summary: Apple unveiled the device as it continues its foray into artificial intelligence and tries to prove it can still innovate.

weekly.title: ‘Peace through strength’: Trump Gaza plan gains global backing one year on
weekly.summary: Donald Trump's Board of Peace excludes UNRWA from Gaza's future as the EU pledges $1 billion and demilitarization efforts gain global momentum.

weekly.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after surgeons remove part of right lung, Vatican says
weekly.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived at Gemelli Hospital in Rome for lung nodule removal after doctors said the growth was identified at a "very early stage." Doctors later confirmed he had a form of lung cancer.

weekly.title: NATO warns Russia: 'We will break' forces, destroy 'anything and everything' if you attack
weekly.summary: Gen. Alexus Grynkewich outlined NATO's strategy to "block, blunt and break" enemy forces at the Warsaw Security Forum amid rising Russia tensions.

weekly.title: British adventurer returns home after 28-year walk around the world
weekly.summary: Adventurer Karl Bushby swam the English Channel and celebrated with fish and chips after his 28-year, 30,000-mile walk from Chile to England.

weekly.title: Is Universal Basic Income the Answer to A.I.-Fueled Job Losses?
weekly.summary: For more than a year, The New York Times followed recipients of universal basic income programs, which Elon Musk and other tech leaders have promoted as a solution to A.I.-fueled job losses.

weekly.title: Meta Unveils New Series of Advanced A.I. Models
weekly.summary: The new models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, are meant to compete with cutting-edge A.I. models from rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI.

weekly.title: Zelenskyy accuses Putin of defying Trump's ceasefire push, sends pointed message to White House
weekly.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy accuses Vladimir Putin of attacking Ukraine's gas infrastructure hours after Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire.

weekly.title: Elon Musk, Delta Airlines and a Feud Over In-Flight Wi-Fi
weekly.summary: Mr. Musk, whose company SpaceX owns Starlink, has attacked the top executive of Delta Air Lines for not selecting the internet provider.

weekly.title: Benjamin Netanyahu's legacy and political future on the line in Israel's Oct 27 election
weekly.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu fights for his legacy in Israel's Oct. 27 vote, the first since the Oct. 7 Hamas massacre reshaped the political landscape.

weekly.title: Pope Leo denounces death penalty as 'inadmissible' ahead of Pentagon's planned livestreamed execution
weekly.summary: Pope Leo XIV called the death penalty "inadmissible" on World Day Against the Death Penalty after the Pentagon announced plans to livestream an execution.

weekly.title: At least 139 migrants dead, 84 missing after overcrowded boat capsizes off Djibouti
weekly.summary: More than 80 people survived the deadly crossing from Djibouti toward Yemen, while at least 84 remained missing as authorities worked to verify additional victims.

weekly.title: Houthis kill 14 at Saudi airport as expert warns of 'rapid targets' amid Middle East war
weekly.summary: Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi Arabian airports in Riyadh and Dammam, killing at least 14 and injuring over 300 as experts warn of wider war.

weekly.title: Trump Russia deal could fuel Putin's war, ex-NATO commander warns as Zelenskyy says 'nyet'
weekly.summary: Donald Trump's energy ceasefire could hand Vladimir Putin fresh revenue to fuel Russia's war in Ukraine, former NATO commander Breedlove warns.

weekly.title: Mojtaba Khamenei defies ‘malicious’ attacks as US Army zeroes in on Iran’s 350,000 troops
weekly.summary: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed U.S. and Israeli strikes failed to weaken Iran's military, as the U.S. Army released a new threat guide.

weekly.title: The Times’s New Space Editor Has Her Eye on the Cosmos
weekly.summary: On the Science desk, Victoria Jaggard spends her days pondering the universe’s most pressing mysteries.

weekly.title: Abbas delays Palestinian elections again, making more than two decades without vote
weekly.summary: Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas delayed elections to 2027, extending a nearly 20-year wait as Israel and Hamas clash over the blame.

weekly.title: Pope Leo announces tumor on lung, surgery planned in 'next few days'
weekly.summary: Pope Leo XIV announced doctors found a lung nodule at a "very early stage," with surgery scheduled in coming days.

weekly.title: Three Mark Zuckerbergs, Three Surprisingly Different Men
weekly.summary: Jeremy Strong in “The Social Reckoning,” Jesse Eisenberg in “The Social Network” and the real Meta executive are all playing parts. But only one has changed his approach.

weekly.title: Justice Dept. Is Investigating TV Networks Over Trump Pool Coverage
weekly.summary: Major TV networks were notified on Friday that the department was examining whether they violated antitrust laws when they suspended pool coverage of President Trump.

weekly.title: Anthropic Agents Tried to Fill Out Visa Forms on State Dept. Website
weekly.summary: The Philadelphia Police Department said the agents had also sent in a false homicide tip. The incidents led the White House to call for better disclosure of rogue A.I. behavior.

developing.title: Live Updates: Students Rally in France for Second Day of Mass Protests in a Week
developing.summary: Just over 150 high schools were closed, and France’s education minister invited three major student groups to meet with him on Thursday afternoon.

developing.title: Live Updates: Human Rights Lawyer Navi Pillay Is Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
developing.summary: Ms. Pillay has served as a judge in her native South Africa and on international courts investigating war crimes. She led a U.N. panel that determined that Israel had committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, a finding the Israeli government rejected.
